title: ldexp uses only the low 32 bits of the exponent
summary: `ldexp x n` uses only the low 32 bits of `n`: `ldexp 1.0 (1 lsl 32)` is 1.0 and `ldexp 1.0 (1 lsl 31)` is 0.0. `Float32.ldexp`, `Float32_u.ldexp` and `Float_u.ldexp` do the same.
cause: The runtime gives the exponent to C's `ldexp` (`ldexpf`) as an `int` (`runtime/floats.c`, `runtime/float32.c`).
